framework: AWS Security Best Practices + HackTricks Cloud AWS
description: SQS/SNS policies, injection, and exfiltration persistence checks

items.title: SQS queue policy uses aws:PrincipalOrgID backdoor-style access
items.description: Org-scoped access via aws:PrincipalOrgID can create hidden broad access paths.
items.remediation: Review SQS queue policies and restrict principals explicitly; avoid org-wide broad permissions unless required.

pci_dss.reason: Least privilege for access to sensitive systems and data flows.

items.title: SQS redrive configuration could enable DLQ-based exfiltration
items.description: DLQ/RedrivePolicy and RedriveAllowPolicy can be abused to siphon messages to attacker-controlled queues.
items.remediation: Lock down who can modify queue attributes; review DLQ targets and allow policies; enforce KMS and tight key policies.

pci_dss.reason: Monitoring of changes and access to messaging systems helps detect exfiltration paths.

items.title: SNS to SQS injection risk via permissive queue/topic policies
items.description: Permissive SNS/SQS policies can allow untrusted publishers to inject messages into trusted queues.
items.remediation: Restrict queue policies to specific SNS topic ARNs with aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount conditions.

pci_dss.reason: Protect public-facing components and validate trusted integrations to prevent injection.

items.title: Unmonitored message move tasks could enable DLQ data theft
items.description: DLQ message move operations can rapidly exfiltrate accumulated messages if abused.
items.remediation: Restrict SQS administrative permissions; monitor CloudTrail for message move operations; encrypt DLQs with KMS.

pci_dss.reason: Time-synchronized audit logging and monitoring support detection of abnormal administrative actions.

notes: Messaging is region-scoped. Findings should include evidence_refs into queue/topic attributes and policies.
